description: Flake triage queue and quarantine ledger for packages/core (and cross-system trading/learning tests). Quarantined tests are excluded from the default vitest run; run them via the escape commands below.

quarantineRule.definition: A test is quarantined when it (a) poisons the suite exit code, (b) silently passes due to env conditions the CI cannot guarantee, or (c) has been observed failing intermittently ≥2 times in 14 days with no fix committed.
quarantineRule.effect: Listed in vitest.config.ts test.exclude. Run with FLAKE_SUITE=1 or by explicit path.
quarantineRule.reviewCadence: Weekly. Move status from 'triage' → 'quarantined' or 'fixed' within 7 days of first observation.

signal.name: flake_quarantine_rate
signal.description: Ratio of quarantined entries to total entries. Target: 0%. Acceptable: <10%. Alert when any entry stays in 'triage' status >7 days.
signal.query: cat packages/core/flake-registry.json | jq '.entries | {total: length, quarantined: [.[] | select(.status=="quarantined")] | length, triage: [.[] | select(.status=="triage")] | length, watch: [.[] | select(.status=="watch")] | length}'
signal.deadline_check: cat packages/core/flake-registry.json | jq --arg today "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)" '.entries | [.[] | select(.deadline != null and .deadline < $today)] | {overdue_count: length, overdue: [.[] | {id, file, deadline, status}]}'
signal.notes: ngt-0350 adversarial pass: added deadline_check signal; triage entries with deadlines must not slip silently. Watch entries have no deadline — they are monitored but don't block CI.

entries.summary: consumePromise had no rejection handler when vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync fired the SLA timeout; Node flagged it unhandled, making full core suite exit 1
entries.rootCause: async generator consumed in a fire-and-forget pattern; SLA timeout rejection fired during vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync before the expect().rejects assertion was attached two lines later. Fixed in 9c18ecf by attaching the rejects assertion synchronously right after creating the promise.
entries.impact: HIGH — broke CI green signal for entire core suite on every run (pre-fix). Quarantined as monitoring hold: regression would re-poison the suite.
entries.fix: DONE (9c18ecf). Promoted to status:watch pending 30 consecutive clean CI runs, then removable from exclude list.

entries.summary: Tests skip silently when ZARAA_RUN_NATIVE_VEC_TESTS is unset; native turbo binding path is never verified in CI
entries.rootCause: Line 18: `const itNative = RUN_NATIVE ? it : it.skip` — env gate with no assertion that native path was exercised in the run. Compounding bug: this entry's own documented runWith command used a different env var name (RUN_NATIVE) than the code checks (ZARAA_RUN_NATIVE_VEC_TESTS) and omitted FLAKE_SUITE=1 (required — this file is in vitest.config.ts's quarantine exclude list); reproduced by running the old documented command, which silently reports '3 passed | 3 skipped' (exit 0) with zero native assertions executed.
entries.impact: MEDIUM — false-green in CI; native binding regressions go undetected
entries.fix: Fixed the runWith command (correct env var + FLAKE_SUITE=1). Added nativeExercisedCount + assertNativePathExercised() suite-level guard (afterAll) so a native run with zero exercised native assertions fails loudly instead of reporting false-green. Verified: FLAKE_SUITE=1 run (native off) -> 6 passed/3 skipped as expected; FLAKE_SUITE=1 ZARAA_RUN_NATIVE_VEC_TESTS=1 run -> 9 passed, native path genuinely exercised on this machine; guard's throw/no-throw branches are directly unit-tested (3 tests) independent of native build availability. Promoted to status:watch pending 30 consecutive clean CI runs, then removable from exclude list (same as flake-001).

entries.summary: Live trade test sets slippageBps:0 — sign error vs production path; paper and live slippage models diverge silently
entries.rootCause: Test fixture uses slippageBps:0 for live path; production adds slippage; difference masks live P&L calculation errors in CI
entries.impact: MEDIUM — CI passes but live trades have miscalculated costs
entries.fix: Set slippageBps to a non-zero realistic value in the live fixture, assert that live P&L includes slippage.
entries.note: Live fixture now uses slippageBps:5 (both legs); asserts live round-trip P&L is strictly less than a zero-slippage expectation and the gap equals the modeled slippage + fee delta.

entries.summary: Retry delay sleepFn zeroed in tests; backoff timing correctness never verified against production windows
entries.rootCause: manager.sleepFn = vi.fn() removes all delay; real production retry windows (500ms–30s exponential) are untested
entries.impact: LOW-MEDIUM — retry logic is exercised, timing is not; production outage recovery may behave differently under real latency
entries.fix: Add a separate timing-realistic test that uses real delays (or vi.useFakeTimers) and asserts actual backoff window values.
entries.note: Added a 'backoff timing windows' describe: under vi.useFakeTimers() it wraps the real production sleep to record requested delays, drives them via vi.runAllTimersAsync(), and asserts rate-limit exponential [1000,2000] and network linear [500,500], all within the 500ms–30s production window.

entries.summary: Unmatched keyword routes return generic default response silently; simulation tests may pass on wrong model behavior
entries.rootCause: routePrompt() has implicit fallback; prompts not matching any keyword pattern trigger default response with no assertion or warning
entries.impact: LOW — simulation tests pass but may not be testing the intended path; could mask model routing regressions
entries.fix: Export MOCK_LLM_DEFAULT_RESPONSE constant; in afterEach assert zero unmatched routes during that test run.
entries.note: DONE: mock-llm.ts now exports MOCK_LLM_DEFAULT_RESPONSE, counts unmatched routePrompt() fall-throughs, and exports getUnmatchedRouteCount()/resetUnmatchedRouteCount() (reset per createMockLlmFn call); 48hr-simulation.test.ts afterEach asserts getUnmatchedRouteCount()===0. Kept status:watch for monitoring.

entries.summary: useFakeTimers at line 768 has no paired useRealTimers within same it block; cleanup relies solely on top-level afterEach at line 126
entries.rootCause: Nested describe at ~L750 calls vi.useFakeTimers() inside an it body without calling vi.useRealTimers() before the test ends; the sole cleanup path is the describe-level afterEach. If that afterEach throws, subsequent tests in the same worker see fake time.
entries.impact: LOW — afterEach backstop exists; risk only triggers if afterEach itself fails
entries.fix: Add vi.useRealTimers() at end of the it block at L768, or add a dedicated afterEach to the enclosing describe for defense in depth.
entries.note: DONE: added an in-block vi.useRealTimers() at the end of the 'start/stop controls polling' it (formerly ~L768) so a throwing describe-level afterEach can't leak fake time into the next test. Kept status:watch.

entries.summary: BUG-2 describe uses real setTimeout(r, 50) inside mock createOrder to simulate concurrent overlap; test outcome depends on wall-clock delivery of 50ms on potentially loaded CI
entries.rootCause: Line 218: mock createOrder does `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 50))` with real timers; if the machine is loaded, both calls may resolve before the mutex is acquired, potentially changing whether the TOCTOU race is detected
entries.impact: LOW-MEDIUM — partially mitigated by maxConcurrency:1 in trading vitest config; still a timing-dependent assertion in a correctness-critical path
entries.fix: Replace setTimeout(r, 50) with a vi.useFakeTimers()-controlled delay, or use a mutex-test helper that doesn't depend on wall-clock overlap.
entries.note: DONE: BUG-2 mock createOrder no longer awaits a wall-clock setTimeout(50); it yields a fixed count of microtask ticks so the concurrency window is machine-load-independent. Serialization is enforced by the per-symbol mutex, not the delay. Kept status:watch.
